ledger.x: c. 424 BC: Samnites take Capua. 'In about 424 BC, Capua was captured by the Samnites'; the Etruscan city, founded about 600 BC by Cato's count, becomes the head of the Campanians. The page does not mention a 438 BC date or a league by name.
343 BC: Capua puts itself under Rome.
216 BC: Capua goes over to Hannibal after Cannae.
211 BC: the Campanian state of Capua ends.

wars.name: First Samnite War
wars.outcome: Capua and Campania placed themselves under Rome's protection against the Samnites; Rome fought at Mount Gaurus and Suessula (disputed) and made peace with the Samnites in 341, keeping its dominating position in Campania.

wars.name: Siege of Capua (211 BC)
wars.outcome: Roman victory: Capua fell despite Hannibal's march on Rome; its institutions abolished and its territory made ager publicus.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the Volturnus plain and the dependent towns are the only markers.
